prompt: Object P moves directly from X to Z in 12 s. Object Q follows a longer route from X to Y to Z in 9 s. Which quantity must be the same for both complete journeys?

answer.explanation: C. Both objects have the same displacement because they share the same start and finish positions.

distractor_explanations: Option 1 is incorrect because Q travels along a longer path (X to Y to Z) than P (X to Z).
Option 2 is incorrect because the distances and times are different for P and Q.
Option 3 is correct because displacement depends only on the initial point X and final point Z, which are identical for both objects.
Option 4 is incorrect because average velocity = displacement / time, and the journey times differ (12 s vs 9 s).
hints: Separate quantities that depend on the route from quantities that depend only on start and finish.
Both objects start at X and finish at Z, but their distances and times differ.
solution: C. Both objects have the same displacement because they share the same start and finish positions.
teacher_walkthrough: Distance depends on the route, so P and Q do not have to travel the same distance.
Average speed uses distance and time. Both can differ here.
Displacement depends only on the change from X to Z, so it is the same for both objects.
Average velocity uses displacement divided by time. The times differ, so the average velocities differ. Therefore C is correct.
